title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 34-37): Grothendieck wants to show that an 'atelier' can be encoded by purely order-theoretic data on its set M of elementary forms. An atelier is his axiomatic setting for a tame or combinatorial topology, given by axioms At 1-7, AtL 1-3 and AtCL. On M he keeps three relations: the order ≤ ('is a closed part of'), a relation ≪ (a kind of 'interior' or strict relation), and a compatibility or 'parallel' relation ∥ coming from the level L of points. On the previous page he forms Φ, the set of subsets of M that are (a) finite for ≤, presumably finitely generated lower sets, and (b) made of pairwise compatible elements. Φ is ordered by inclusion, with F ≪ G iff every X in F has some Y in G with X ≪ Y. The basic closed sets X̃ = M_{≤X} lie in Φ. A 'figure' is a subfamily 𝓕 ⊂ Φ satisfying: (i) 𝓕 is closed downward under closed parts; (ii) 𝓕 is closed under unions of compatible members, i.e. whenever F ∪ G ∈ Φ. In other words 𝓕 is a kind of ideal in Φ for compatible joins.

This page adds (iii): 𝓕 contains the elementary figures, written {{X}}, presumably the X̃ for X ∈ M. With (i) and (ii), 𝓕 then contains every closed part of every finite union of X̃'s. He claims the converse: any 𝓕 satisfying (i)-(iii) satisfies the conditions wanted of a figure in the atelier. The figures are all of finite type iff (a) 𝓕 = 𝓕_0, the family of finite unions of X̃'s, which 'gives nothing new', and (b) every closed part of an X̃ is of finite type for ≤.

Conclusion: apart from a small vagueness caused by possibly infinite figures, the atelier is entirely expressed by the structure (M, ≤, ≪, ∥). Here ∥ is defined via L 'sans plus', and the structure satisfies the axioms ML 1-ML 4, plus ML 0. The next page states this is equivalent to giving the atelier axioms. It adds axiom ML 6 for when ∥ is given on M rather than L, and a polyhedral variant (ML 0 pol), in which intervals of M_{≤X} have finite infs.

The page thus serves a reconstruction or representation theorem: atelier ≃ ordered set with extra relations. Figures are recovered as 'compatible ideals' generated by elementary forms, much as a regular CW or polyhedral complex is recovered from its face poset.
errors: Slight redundancy or imprecision in the finite-type criterion. By (i)+(iii), every 𝓕 already contains all closed parts of the X̃. So 'all figures of finite type' forces condition (b) and then 𝓕 = 𝓕_0. Condition (a) is more a consequence than an independent condition, unless elements of Φ are already assumed of finite type.

The notation {{X}} in (iii) is ambiguous. Read literally as a family whose only member is the singleton {X}, downward closure under inclusion would not yield 'all closed parts of finite unions of X̃'. It must denote the elementary figure generated by X̃. Grothendieck himself flags the issue of infinite figures as 'un petit flottement'.

ideas.what: Reconstructing a topological or combinatorial 'atelier' from the poset of elementary forms with relations ≤, ≪, ∥ (axioms ML 0-ML 4)
ideas.modern_name: Face-poset reconstruction (regular CW / polyhedral complexes from their face posets); combinatorial models for tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face posets of regular CW complexes: Björner (1984) and earlier folklore; tame topology: van den Dries and others
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only called for programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'atelier' axiomatics appear only in these unpublished Analysis situs notes, as far as I know

ideas.what: Figures as subfamilies of Φ closed downward and under compatible unions, containing the generators
ideas.modern_name: Ideals in a poset / clique (flag) complex of a compatibility relation; ideal completion

ideas.what: Lifting ≪ to finite sets by F ≪ G iff ∀X∈F ∃Y∈G with X ≪ Y
ideas.modern_name: Hoare (lower) powerdomain lifting of a way-below / auxiliary relation; abstract bases in domain theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plotkin, Smyth (1976-78); Abramsky-Jung (1994) for abstract bases

ideas.what: Finite-type criterion: figures all of finite type iff they are finite unions of X̃ and closed parts of X̃ are finitely generated
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness / coherence condition (cf. coherent posets, finitely generated lower sets)

missed.claim: The encoding uses a poset with an auxiliary strict relation ≪, its Hoare-style lift to finite compatible sets, and recovery of the structure by ideals. This is formally the same machinery as abstract bases and round-ideal completion in domain theory, and as the coherence-space/clique construction in linear logic. Grothendieck develops it in parallel for tame topology with no link to that literature.
missed.quote: F ≪ G ⟺ ∀X ∈ F, ∃Y ∈ G tel que X ≪ Y ... tout s'exprime par (M, ≤, ≪, ∥)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Domain-theoretic and point-free tools (continuous posets, locales from bases) could be applied to the 'atelier' framework for tame topology, or vice versa. This is a modest connection, likely noticed by anyone versed in both fields.

missed.claim: Grothendieck admits a 'petit flottement' about infinite figures. The equivalence atelier ↔ (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) satisfying ML 0-ML 4 is only clean in the finite-type case, and the infinite case is left unresolved here.
missed.quote: À part donc un petit flottement dû à la possibilité de figures infinies
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A precise statement would be an ind-completion or locale-type equivalence for combinatorial tame topology. It is unclear whether it was ever settled.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step of an order-theoretic representation theorem inside the little-known 'atelier' axiomatics. The framework itself is unpublished and of historical interest, but this page's content (ideals in a poset of compatible finite sets) is standard. The domain-theory parallel is mild.
transcription_corrections: 'figures dimensionnelles[?]' should likely read 'figures élémentaires' (matches 'formes élémentaires' on p. 35).
In (iii) the image appears to read '∀X ∈ M, {{X}} ∈ 𝓕' with a capital X inside the braces.
'(ce qui ne donne une notion que rien de nouveau de plus' is more plausibly '(ce qui ne donne rien de nouveau de plus)'.
'(pour ≤)' is an insertion after 'toute partie fermée d'un X̃ est de type fini'.
'À part donc un petit flottement dû : la possibilité' should be 'dû à la possibilité de figures infinies'; 'on voit que tous s'exprimer' should be 'on voit que tout s'exprime'.
The axioms are named 'ML 1 – ML 4' and '(ML 0)' (cf. ML 6, ML 0 pol on p. 37), not 'M 1 – M 4' and '(M 0)'.
'il faut et il suffit [?]' is clearly 'il faut et il suffit'.
